correctness.rationale: The journal PDF confirms the exact ODE in Eq. (2.1), the printed denominator μ(B+μ) in Eq. (2.4), the no-positive-equilibrium assertion immediately following it, and the global stability assertion in Theorem 4.1. The I row of the full Jacobian at (B/η,0,0) has only the diagonal entry MB/η−(μ+η), giving the threshold in the Finding. For the full perturbation the remainder includes a mixed I(S−B/η) term; the proof's O(I²) notation is valid along S=B/η and does not affect the Jacobian argument. Summing the equations gives N'=B−ηN. At an endemic equilibrium R=μI/(α+η) and S=(μ+η)/[M(1+γI)], so N=B/η gives exactly the reported quadratic. For 0<ℛ<1 its leading and constant terms are positive. Positivity of the root sum and discriminant require z=Bγ/k>1 and (z−1)²>4z(1−ℛ)/ℛ; the upper discriminant root gives the strict reported bound (equality gives one double root). S and R are positive upon back-substitution. At the witness both thresholds are 1/2. In coordinates (N,I,R) the independently checked characteristic factors are (x+1)²(x+2), (x+1)(36x²+43x−42)/36, and (x+1)(5x²+12x+14)/5: respectively all negative eigenvalues, opposite-sign quadratic roots, and a conjugate pair with negative real part. The two attracting equilibria are local statements; even the constant trajectory at either positive equilibrium refutes global attraction. Replay: `python3 /workspace/branches/independent-checks.py 3` (SymPy exact substitutions); the uploaded checker was read, not run. No general basin or phase portrait follows.

value.rationale: It corrects a consequential qualitative claim in a published ODE and separates the bad invasion formula from genuine subthreshold bistability. The all-positive exact witness with both thresholds equal eliminates a natural alternative explanation of the contradiction. The sharp multiplicity condition gives more than an isolated example; the result is mathematical and does not assert a real-world transmission conclusion.
